text:
Ottawa trailed 2-0 after the first period and still won the shootout, which fits how the game was actually played. NSH scored twice on chances worth 20 and 9 percent (Ross Colton at even strength, Jonathan Marchessault on the power play), then watched the OTT attack take over. In the second period OTT out-chanced NSH 1.16 to 0.12 in expected goals, and Tim Stützle cut the lead to 2-1 on a power-play wrist shot.

The equalizer came with 1:23 left in regulation. Drake Batherson deflected one in at 18:37 of the third, set up by Shane Pinto and Stützle. OTT finished with 65 shot attempts to NSH's 47 and 2.82 expected goals to 2.06, which gave the home side a 69 percent share of simulated replays. At even strength it was close, 1.51 for NSH and 1.44 for OTT, so the edge came from special teams. OTT's power plays generated 1.03 expected goals while NSH's produced 0.25, each side going 1 for 6.

Matt Murray was the reason NSH reached the shootout, stopping 18 of 20 shots against 2.82 expected goals against, 0.82 goals saved above expected. Linus Ullmark let in two goals on 1.77 expected, a little worse than the model predicted. In the shootout Ryan O'Reilly beat Ullmark for NSH, but Stützle and Pinto both scored for OTT while Filip Forsberg and Steven Stamkos were stopped. Stützle, with a goal and an assist across 26:06, took first star.
